title: Sufficiency and gospel vocation granted; eternal will to save the reprobate without the Spirit's special work denied
pass_a_gloss: It was also supposed, as if the Reformed deny either the sufficiency of Christ's Redemption, or even its extension to all or to the whole World; Which we freely grant, but in the sense of Holy Scripture as to all who are to be brought into glory, even any at all, through the whole World, with no distinction under the Economy of the N.T. So neither do the Reformed deny the Vocation which is made through the Ministers of the Gospel, general, promiscuous, no one excluded; But they deny the eternal will of God of saving & redeeming even the reprobate (whom the Lutherans acknowledge as such according to foreknowledge) without the special and efficacious Operation of the Holy Spirit — which is established as impossible by themselves, from their concessions. Who then, unless that harsh Fellow-servant, would eternally damn those who deny these things in this sense?
pass_b_english: It was also supposed that the Reformed deny either the sufficiency of Christ's redemption, or even its extension to all — or to the whole world. That we freely grant, but in Holy Scripture's sense: as to all who are to be brought into glory, even any at all, throughout the whole world, with no distinction under the New Testament economy.

So the Reformed do not deny the vocation that comes through the ministers of the Gospel — general, promiscuous, no one excluded. But they do deny an eternal will of God to save and redeem even the reprobate (whom the Lutherans themselves acknowledge as such according to foreknowledge) without the Holy Spirit's special and efficacious operation — which, from their own concessions, they have already granted is impossible.
Who then, unless that harsh fellow-servant, would damn forever those who deny these things in this sense?
source_text: Suppositum etiam fuit, quasi Reformati Redemptionis Christi aut sufficientiam negent, aut extensionem etiam ad omnes vel ad totum Mundum; Quod sanè largimur, sed in sensu Scripturae S. quoad omnes in gloriam adducendos, etiam quosvis, per totum Mundum, nullo discrimine sub Oeconomia N. T. Ità nec Vocationem negant Reformati, quae fit per Ministros Evangelii, generalem, promiscuam, nemine excluso; Cæterùm negant voluntatem Dei aeternam servandi & redimendi etiam reprobos (quos Lutherani agnoscunt κατὰ πρόγνωσιν tales) sine speciali efficacique Operatione Spiritus S., praestito ab ipsis impossibili, ex concessis. Quis verò, nisi immitis ille Conservus, aeternum damnet ista hoc sensu negantes?

lemmas.gloss: special efficacious operation of the Holy Spirit

choices.term: praestito ab ipsis impossibili, ex concessis

choices.why: Ablative absolute: without the Spirit's special work, saving reprobates is impossible — already conceded by the Lutheran side
